calls.head: The Capitals get in close, the Hurricanes shoot from distance
calls.body: On shots from in close, Washington is one of the league’s best, but Carolina is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Capitals to do more of their damage around the net.

surprises.head: Washington picked Carolina’s defense apart
surprises.body: Washington usually gets better looks than most teams, and Carolina usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: Washington’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.2% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.5% (about 7.2% against Carolina) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 15 games.

story.head: The Capitals take down the Hurricanes
paras: Alex Tuch made his Capitals debut, after five seasons with the Sabres. Tuch scored twice and Cole Hutson once in just under eight minutes early in the first to put the Capitals up 3-0. Jakob Chychrun made it 4-0 on the power play early in the second, but Sebastian Aho got the Hurricanes on the board on the power play late in the period. Ryan Leonard stretched the lead to 5-1 just 8 seconds later. Logan Stankoven made a dent in Washington’s lead midway through the third, bringing it to 5-2.
The Hurricanes had a little more of the play. The Capitals had the finish. Logan Thompson made 31 saves for the Caps, and Brandon Bussi allowed five goals on 27 shots.
Charles Alexis Legault picked up a ten-minute misconduct. The Capitals improved to 1-0-0, and the Hurricanes dropped to 0-1-1.
